sanskrit: śivena dhyāhi māṃ brahman svasti caiva vadasva me bhavatprasādād icchāmi praveṣṭuṃ durbhidāṃ camūm
english: Think upon me with kindness, O brāhmaṇa, and pronounce your blessing over me. By your grace I wish to penetrate this army that none can break.

sanskrit: bhavān pitṛsamo mahyaṃ dharmarājasamo 'pi ca tathā kṛṣṇasamaś caiva satyam etad bravīmi te
english: You are to me as a father, and as the Dharmarāja as well, and even as Kṛṣṇa himself — this I tell you in truth.

sanskrit: aśvatthāmā yathā tāta rakṣaṇīyas tavānagha tathāham api te rakṣyaḥ sadaiva dvijasattama
english: As Aśvatthāman, dear sir, is one to be guarded by you, O sinless one, so too am I ever to be guarded by you, O best of the twice-born.

sanskrit: tava prasādād icchāmi sindhurājānam āhave nihantuṃ dvipadāṃ śreṣṭha pratijñāṃ rakṣa me vibho
english: By your grace I wish to slay the king of the Sindhus in battle, O best of men; uphold my vow, O mighty one.

sanskrit: evam uktas tadācāryaḥ pratyuvāca smayann iva mām ajitvā na bībhatso śakyo jetuṃ jayadrathaḥ
english: Thus addressed, the preceptor answered, as if smiling: "Without first conquering me, O Bībhatsu, Jayadratha cannot be conquered."

sanskrit: etāvad uktvā taṃ droṇaḥ śaravrātair avākirat sarathāśvadhvajaṃ tīkṣṇaiḥ prahasan vai sasārathim
english: Having said only this much, Droṇa, laughing, covered him over with floods of sharp arrows — together with his chariot, horses, banner, and charioteer.

sanskrit: tato 'rjunaḥ śaravrātān droṇasyāvārya sāyakaiḥ droṇam abhyardayad bāṇair ghorarūpair mahattaraiḥ
english: Then Arjuna, warding off Droṇa's floods of arrows with his own shafts, assailed Droṇa with arrows of dreadful form and greater might.

sanskrit: vivyādha ca raṇe droṇam anumānya viśāṃ pate kṣatradharmaṃ samāsthāya navabhiḥ sāyakaiḥ punaḥ
english: And in the battle, O lord of peoples, having first sought his leave and abiding by the law of the warrior, he pierced Droṇa again with nine shafts.

sanskrit: tasyeṣūn iṣubhiś chittvā droṇo vivyādha tāv ubhau viṣāgnijvalanaprakhyair iṣubhiḥ kṛṣṇapāṇḍavau
english: Cutting down his arrows with arrows of his own, Droṇa pierced them both — Kṛṣṇa and the Pāṇḍava — with shafts that blazed like poison and fire.

sanskrit: iyeṣa pāṇḍavas tasya bāṇaiś chettuṃ śarāsanam tasya cintayatas tv evaṃ phalgunasya mahātmanaḥ droṇaḥ śarair asaṃbhrānto jyāṃ cicchedāśu vīryavān
english: The Pāṇḍava sought to sever Droṇa's bow with his arrows; but while the great-souled Phalguna was still pondering thus, the valiant Droṇa, unflustered, swiftly cut the bowstring with his shafts.

sanskrit: vivyādha ca hayān asya dhvajaṃ sārathim eva ca arjunaṃ ca śarair vīraṃ smayamāno 'bhyavākirat
english: And he pierced his horses, his banner, and his charioteer too, and, smiling, the hero covered Arjuna over with his shafts.

sanskrit: etasminn antare pārthaḥ sajjaṃ kṛtvā mahad dhanuḥ viśeṣayiṣyann ācāryaṃ sarvāstraviduṣāṃ varam mumoca ṣaṭśatān bāṇān gṛhītvaikam iva drutam
english: In that interval Pārtha, stringing his great bow afresh and bent on surpassing the preceptor, foremost of all who know the weapons, loosed six hundred arrows swiftly, as though he had taken but one.

sanskrit: punaḥ sapta śatān anyān sahasraṃ cānivartinām cikṣepāyutaśaś cānyāṃs te 'ghnan droṇasya tāṃ camūm
english: Again he hurled seven hundred more, and a thousand unswerving shafts, and others by tens of thousands; and they slew that host of Droṇa's.

sanskrit: taiḥ samyag astair balinā kṛtinā citrayodhinā manuṣyavājimātaṅgā viddhāḥ petur gatāsavaḥ
english: By those well-aimed weapons of that strong, skilled, and many-wiled fighter, men, horses, and elephants, pierced through, fell down with their lives gone.

sanskrit: vidrutāś ca raṇe petuḥ saṃchinnāyudhajīvitāḥ rathino rathamukhyebhyaḥ sahayāḥ śarapīḍitāḥ
english: And the chariot-warriors, their weapons and their lives cut short, fell scattered in the battle from their foremost cars, their horses with them, tormented by his arrows.

sanskrit: cūrṇitākṣiptadagdhānāṃ vajrānilahutāśanaiḥ tulyarūpā gajāḥ petur giryagrāmbudaveśmanām
english: Like things pulverized, hurled down, and burnt by the thunderbolt, the wind, and the fire, the elephants fell, resembling the cloud-wreathed mansions upon mountain peaks.

sanskrit: petur aśvasahasrāṇi prahatāny arjuneṣubhiḥ haṃsā himavataḥ pṛṣṭhe vāriviprahatā iva
english: Thousands of horses fell, struck down by Arjuna's arrows, like geese upon the ridge of Himavat beaten down by rain.

sanskrit: rathāśvadvipapattyoghāḥ salilaughā ivādbhutāḥ yugāntādityaraśmyābhaiḥ pāṇḍavāstaśarair hatāḥ
english: The floods of chariots, horses, elephants, and foot-soldiers, wondrous as floods of water, were slain by the Pāṇḍava's arrows that shone like the sun's rays at the end of an age.

sanskrit: taṃ pāṇḍavādityaśarāṃśujālaṃ; kurupravīrān yudhi niṣṭapantam sa droṇameghaḥ śaravarṣavegaiḥ; prācchādayan megha ivārkaraśmīn
english: That net of arrow-beams from the Pāṇḍava-sun, scorching the Kuru champions in the fight, the cloud that was Droṇa veiled over with the rush of its arrow-showers, as a cloud veils the rays of the sun.

sanskrit: athātyarthavisṛṣṭena dviṣatām asubhojinā ājaghne vakṣasi droṇo nārācena dhanaṃjayam
english: Then with an iron shaft loosed with surpassing force, a feeder upon the lives of foes, Droṇa struck Dhanaṃjaya upon the breast.

sanskrit: sa vihvalitasarvāṅgaḥ kṣitikampe yathācalaḥ dhairyam ālambya bībhatsur droṇaṃ vivyādha patribhiḥ
english: His whole frame shaken, like a mountain in an earthquake, Bībhatsu, taking hold of his steadiness, pierced Droṇa with feathered shafts.

sanskrit: droṇas tu pañcabhir bāṇair vāsudevam atāḍayat arjunaṃ ca trisaptatyā dhvajaṃ cāsya tribhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: But Droṇa struck Vāsudeva with five arrows, and Arjuna with seventy-three, and his banner with three shafts.

sanskrit: viśeṣayiṣyañ śiṣyaṃ ca droṇo rājan parākramī adṛśyam arjunaṃ cakre nimeṣāc charavṛṣṭibhiḥ
english: And bent on outdoing his pupil, the valiant Droṇa, O king, made Arjuna invisible in the twinkling of an eye with showers of arrows.

sanskrit: prasaktān patato 'drākṣma bhāradvājasya sāyakān maṇḍalīkṛtam evāsya dhanuś cādṛśyatādbhutam
english: We saw the shafts of Bhāradvāja falling in unbroken streams, and his bow, bent into a perfect circle, was a wondrous sight to behold.

sanskrit: te 'bhyayuḥ samare rājan vāsudevadhanaṃjayau droṇasṛṣṭāḥ subahavaḥ kaṅkapatraparicchadāḥ
english: They sped toward Vāsudeva and Dhanaṃjaya in the battle, O king — those very many shafts loosed by Droṇa, fledged with heron feathers.

sanskrit: tad dṛṣṭvā tādṛśaṃ yuddhaṃ droṇapāṇḍavayos tadā vāsudevo mahābuddhiḥ kāryavattām acintayat
english: Seeing such a combat then between Droṇa and the Pāṇḍava, Vāsudeva of great wisdom bethought himself of what must be done.

sanskrit: tato 'bravīd vāsudevo dhanaṃjayam idaṃ vacaḥ pārtha pārtha mahābāho na naḥ kālātyayo bhavet
english: Then Vāsudeva spoke this word to Dhanaṃjaya: "Pārtha, Pārtha, O mighty-armed, let no waste of our time befall us.

sanskrit: droṇam utsṛjya gacchāmaḥ kṛtyam etan mahattaram pārthaś cāpy abravīt kṛṣṇaṃ yatheṣṭam iti keśava
english: Leaving Droṇa aside, let us go on; the task before us is far greater." And Pārtha too said to Kṛṣṇa, "As you wish, O Keśava."

sanskrit: tataḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā droṇaṃ prāyān mahābhujaḥ parivṛttaś ca bībhatsur agacchad visṛjañ śarān
english: Then the mighty-armed one, having circled Droṇa to the right, went on; and Bībhatsu, wheeling about, advanced, loosing his arrows.

sanskrit: tato 'bravīt smayan droṇaḥ kvedaṃ pāṇḍava gamyate nanu nāma raṇe śatrum ajitvā na nivartase
english: Then Droṇa said, smiling: "Whither do you go, O Pāṇḍava? Surely you do not turn back without first conquering your foe in battle?"

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca gurur bhavān na me śatruḥ śiṣyaḥ putrasamo 'smi te na cāsti sa pumāṃl loke yas tvāṃ yudhi parājayet
english: Arjuna said: You are my teacher, not my foe; I am your pupil, like a son to you. Nor is there any man in this world who could vanquish you in battle.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca evaṃ bruvāṇo bībhatsur jayadrathavadhotsukaḥ tvarāyukto mahābāhus tat sainyaṃ samupādravat
english: Saṃjaya said: Speaking thus, Bībhatsu, eager for the slaying of Jayadratha, the mighty-armed one, in haste fell upon that host.

sanskrit: taṃ cakrarakṣau pāñcālyau yudhāmanyūttamaujasau anvayātāṃ mahātmānau viśantaṃ tāvakaṃ balam
english: As he entered your forces, the two Pāñcāla guardians of his chariot-wheels, the great-souled Yudhāmanyu and Uttamaujas, followed close behind him.

sanskrit: tato jayo mahārāja kṛtavarmā ca sāttvataḥ kāmbojaś ca śrutāyuś ca dhanaṃjayam avārayan
english: Then, O great king, Jaya and Kṛtavarman of the Sāttvatas, and the Kāmboja, and Śrutāyus, withstood Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ daśasahasrāṇi rathānām anuyāyinām abhīṣāhāḥ śūrasenāḥ śibayo 'tha vasātayaḥ
english: In their following were ten thousand chariot-warriors — the Abhīṣāhas, the Śūrasenas, the Śibis, and the Vasātis,

sanskrit: mācellakā lalitthāś ca kekayā madrakās tathā nārāyaṇāś ca gopālāḥ kāmbojānāṃ ca ye gaṇāḥ
english: the Mācellakas and the Lalitthas, the Kekayas and the Madrakas, the Nārāyaṇa cowherds, and those clans that are the Kāmbojas' —

sanskrit: karṇena vijitāḥ pūrvaṃ saṃgrāme śūrasaṃmatāḥ bhāradvājaṃ puraskṛtya tyaktātmāno 'rjunaṃ prati
english: all conquered before by Karṇa, honored as heroes in battle — placing Bhāradvāja at their head and casting away their lives, they advanced against Arjuna.

sanskrit: putraśokābhisaṃtaptaṃ kruddhaṃ mṛtyum ivāntakam tyajantaṃ tumule prāṇān saṃnaddhaṃ citrayodhinam
english: Burning with grief for his son, wrathful as death the all-ender, ready to lay down his life in the tumult, armored, a fighter of many wiles,

sanskrit: gāhamānam anīkāni mātaṅgam iva yūthapam maheṣvāsaṃ parākrāntaṃ naravyāghram avārayan
english: plunging through the ranks like the lord of an elephant herd, the great archer of surpassing valor, that tiger among men — him they withstood.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ tumulaṃ lomaharṣaṇam anyonyaṃ vai prārthayatāṃ yodhānām arjunasya ca
english: Then there arose a tumultuous battle that made the hair stand on end, between those warriors and Arjuna, each striving against the other.

sanskrit: jayadrathavadhaprepsum āyāntaṃ puruṣarṣabham nyavārayanta sahitāḥ kriyā vyādhim ivotthitam
english: As that bull among men came on, longing to slay Jayadratha, they together held him back, as remedies hold back a risen disease.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca saṃniruddhas tu taiḥ pārtho mahābalaparākramaḥ drutaṃ samanuyātaś ca droṇena rathināṃ varaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Though held back by them, Pārtha of mighty strength and valor, foremost of chariot-warriors, was also pursued in haste by Droṇa.

sanskrit: kirann iṣugaṇāṃs tikṣṇān svaraśmīn iva bhāskaraḥ tāpayām āsa tat sainyaṃ dehaṃ vyādhigaṇo yathā
english: Scattering volleys of sharp arrows, as the sun scatters its own rays, he tormented that host as a host of diseases torments the body.

sanskrit: aśvo viddho dhvajaś chinnaḥ sārohaḥ patito gajaḥ chatrāṇi cāpaviddhāni rathāś cakrair vinā kṛtāḥ
english: Horses were pierced, banners cut down, elephants with their riders fell, parasols were struck away, and chariots were left without their wheels.

sanskrit: vidrutāni ca sainyāni śarārtāni samantataḥ ity āsīt tumulaṃ yuddhaṃ na prājñāyata kiṃ cana
english: The armies, afflicted by arrows, fled in all directions; so tumultuous was the battle that nothing whatever could be made out.

sanskrit: teṣām āyacchatāṃ saṃkhye parasparam ajihmagaiḥ arjuno dhvajinīṃ rājann abhīkṣṇaṃ samakampayat
english: As they strove against one another in the battle with straight-flying shafts, Arjuna, O king, made the banner-bearing host tremble again and again.

sanskrit: satyāṃ cikīrṣamāṇas tu pratijñāṃ satyasaṃgaraḥ abhyadravad rathaśreṣṭhaṃ śoṇāśvaṃ śvetavāhanaḥ
english: Seeking to make his vow come true, true to his pledges, the white-steeded one rushed upon that foremost chariot-warrior whose horses were red.

sanskrit: taṃ droṇaḥ pañcaviṃśatyā marmabhidbhir ajihmagaiḥ antevāsinam ācāryo maheṣvāsaṃ samardayat
english: Droṇa the preceptor assailed that great archer, his own pupil, with twenty-five straight-flying shafts that pierced the vital parts.

sanskrit: taṃ tūrṇam iva bībhatsuḥ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ abhyadhāvad iṣūn asyann iṣuvegavighātakān
english: Swiftly Bībhatsu, foremost of all bearers of weapons, charged him, hurling arrows that broke the force of his arrows.

sanskrit: tasyāśu kṣipato bhallān bhallaiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ pratyavidhyad ameyātmā brahmāstraṃ samudīrayan
english: As he swiftly cast his broad-headed shafts, the immeasurable one struck them back with broad-headed shafts of smooth joints, invoking the Brahmā weapon.

sanskrit: tad adbhutam apaśyāma droṇasyācāryakaṃ yudhi yatamāno yuvā nainaṃ pratyavidhyad yad arjunaḥ
english: We beheld that wondrous mastery of Droṇa in the fight — that though the youthful Arjuna strove, he could not strike him back.

sanskrit: kṣarann iva mahāmegho vāridhārāḥ sahasraśaḥ droṇameghaḥ pārthaśailaṃ vavarṣa śaravṛṣṭibhiḥ
english: As a great cloud pours down its streams of water by the thousand, so the cloud that was Droṇa rained showers of arrows upon the mountain that was Pārtha.

sanskrit: arjunaḥ śaravarṣaṃ tad brahmāstreṇaiva māriṣa pratijagrāha tejasvī bāṇair bāṇān viśātayan
english: That rain of arrows, O sire, the radiant Arjuna received with the Brahmā weapon itself, scattering arrows with arrows.

sanskrit: droṇas tu pañcaviṃśatyā śvetavāhanam ārdayat vāsudevaṃ ca saptatyā bāhvor urasi cāśugaiḥ
english: But Droṇa afflicted the white-steeded one with twenty-five swift shafts, and Vāsudeva with seventy, upon the arms and the breast.

sanskrit: pārthas tu prahasan dhīmān ācāryaṃ sa śaraughiṇam visṛjantaṃ śitān bāṇān avārayata taṃ yudhi
english: But the wise Pārtha, laughing, warded off the preceptor in battle as he poured forth floods of arrows, loosing his sharp shafts.

sanskrit: atha tau vadhyamānau tu droṇena rathasattamau āvarjayetāṃ durdharṣaṃ yugāntāgnim ivotthitam
english: Then those two foremost of chariot-warriors, sore beset by Droṇa, turned aside the unassailable one, who had risen like the fire at the end of an age.

sanskrit: varjayan niśitān bāṇān droṇacāpaviniḥsṛtān kirīṭamālī kaunteyo bhojānīkaṃ nyapātayat
english: Avoiding the sharp arrows that issued from Droṇa's bow, the diademed and garlanded son of Kuntī struck down the army of the Bhoja.

sanskrit: so 'ntarā kṛtavarmāṇaṃ kāmbojaṃ ca sudakṣiṇam abhyayād varjayan droṇaṃ mainākam iva parvatam
english: Avoiding Droṇa as one avoids the Maināka mountain, he advanced between Kṛtavarman and the Kāmboja Sudakṣiṇa.

sanskrit: tato bhojo naravyāghraṃ duḥsahaḥ kurusattama avidhyat tūrṇam avyagro daśabhiḥ kaṅkapatribhiḥ
english: Then the Bhoja Duḥsaha, O best of the Kurus, unperturbed, swiftly pierced that tiger among men with ten heron-feathered shafts.

sanskrit: tam arjunaḥ śitenājau rājan vivyādha patriṇā punaś cānyais tribhir bāṇair mohayann iva sātvatam
english: Arjuna pierced him in the fight, O king, with a sharp feathered shaft, and again with three other arrows, as if to bewilder the Sātvata.

sanskrit: bhojas tu prahasan pārthaṃ vāsudevaṃ ca mādhavam ekaikaṃ pañcaviṃśatyā sāyakānāṃ samārpayat
english: But the Bhoja, laughing, planted twenty-five shafts in each — in Pārtha and in Mādhava, that is, Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: tasyārjuno dhanuś chittvā vivyādhainaṃ trisaptabhiḥ śarair agniśikhākāraiḥ kruddhāśīviṣasaṃnibhaiḥ
english: Cutting his bow, Arjuna pierced him with twenty-one arrows shaped like tongues of fire, like enraged venomous serpents.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya kṛtavarmā mahārathaḥ pañcabhiḥ sāyakais tūrṇaṃ vivyādhorasi bhārata
english: Then, taking up another bow, the great chariot-warrior Kṛtavarman swiftly pierced him in the breast with five shafts, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: punaś ca niśitair bāṇaiḥ pārthaṃ vivyādha pañcabhiḥ taṃ pārtho navabhir bāṇair ājaghāna stanāntare
english: And again he pierced Pārtha with five sharp arrows; whereupon Pārtha struck him between the breasts with nine arrows.

sanskrit: viṣaktaṃ dṛśya kaunteyaṃ kṛtavarmarathaṃ prati cintayām āsa vārṣṇeyo na naḥ kālātyayo bhavet
english: Seeing the son of Kuntī held fast against Kṛtavarman's chariot, the Vārṣṇeya reflected: "Let there be no waste of our time."

sanskrit: tataḥ kṛṣṇo 'bravīt pārthaṃ kṛtavarmaṇi mā dayām kurusāṃbandhikaṃ kṛtvā pramathyainaṃ viśātaya
english: Then Kṛṣṇa said to Pārtha: "Show no mercy to Kṛtavarman on the score of kinship with the Kurus; crush and scatter him."

sanskrit: tataḥ sa kṛtavarmāṇaṃ mohayitvārjunaḥ śaraiḥ abhyagāj javanair aśvaiḥ kāmbojānām anīkinīm
english: Then Arjuna, having bewildered Kṛtavarman with his arrows, advanced with his swift horses upon the army of the Kāmbojas.

sanskrit: amarṣitas tu hārdikhyaḥ praviṣṭe śvetavāhane vidhunvan saśaraṃ cāpaṃ pāñcālyābhyāṃ samāgataḥ
english: But the son of Hṛdika, indignant once the white-steeded one had passed within, brandishing his bow with arrow fitted, closed with the two Pāñcālas.

sanskrit: cakrarakṣau tu pāñcālyāv arjunasya padānugau paryavārayad āyāntau kṛtavarmā ratheṣubhiḥ
english: As the two Pāñcāla guardians of Arjuna's wheels, who followed in his track, came on, Kṛtavarman hemmed them in with his chariot-arrows.

sanskrit: tāv avidhyat tato bhojaḥ sarvapāraśavaiḥ śaraiḥ tribhir eva yudhāmanyuṃ caturbhiś cottamaujasam
english: Then the Bhoja pierced them both with arrows wholly of iron — Yudhāmanyu with three, and Uttamaujas with four.

sanskrit: tāv apy enaṃ vivyadhatur daśabhir daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ saṃcicchidatur apy asya dhvajaṃ kārmukam eva ca
english: They too pierced him, each with ten arrows, and they cut asunder both his banner and his bow.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya hārdikyaḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ kṛtvā vidhanuṣau vīrau śaravarṣair avākirat
english: Then the son of Hṛdika, taking up another bow, swooning with rage, having stripped the two heroes of their bows, covered them over with showers of arrows.

sanskrit: tāv anye dhanuṣī sajye kṛtvā bhojaṃ vijaghnatuḥ tenāntareṇa bībhatsur viveśāmitravāhinīm
english: They, taking up two other strung bows, smote the Bhoja; and in that interval Bībhatsu entered the army of his foes.

sanskrit: na lebhāte tu tau dvāraṃ vāritau kṛtavarmaṇā dhārtarāṣṭreṣv anīkeṣu yatamānau nararṣabhau
english: But those two bulls among men, held back by Kṛtavarman, won no opening, though they strove, into the ranks of the Dhārtarāṣṭras.

sanskrit: anīkāny ardayan yuddhe tvaritaḥ śvetavāhanaḥ nāvadhīt kṛtavarmāṇaṃ prāptam apy arisūdanaḥ
english: Afflicting the ranks in the battle, the white-steeded slayer of foes, in his haste, did not slay Kṛtavarman, though he had him within reach.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā tu tathāyāntaṃ śūro rājā śrutāyudhaḥ abhyadravat susaṃkruddho vidhunvāno mahad dhanuḥ
english: Seeing him coming on thus, the heroic king Śrutāyudha, greatly enraged, rushed at him, brandishing his great bow.

sanskrit: sa pārthaṃ tribhir ānarchat saptatyā ca janārdanam kṣurapreṇa sutīkṣṇena pārthaketum atāḍayat
english: He struck Pārtha with three shafts and Janārdana with seventy, and with a keen razor-edged arrow he hit Pārtha's banner.

sanskrit: tam arjuno navatyā tu śarāṇāṃ nataparvaṇām ājaghāna bhṛśaṃ kruddhas tottrair iva mahādvipam
english: Then Arjuna, exceedingly wrathful, struck him with ninety smooth-jointed arrows, as one goads a great elephant with hooks.

sanskrit: sa tan na mamṛṣe rājan pāṇḍaveyasya vikramam athainaṃ saptasaptatyā nārācānāṃ samārpayat
english: He could not brook that prowess of the Pāṇḍava, O king, and so he planted seventy-seven iron shafts in him.

sanskrit: tasyārjuno dhanuś chittvā śarāvāpaṃ nikṛtya ca ājaghānorasi kruddhaḥ saptabhir nataparvabhiḥ
english: Cutting his bow and severing his quiver, the wrathful Arjuna struck him upon the breast with seven smooth-jointed arrows.
